answer: Latency-fingerprint cohort matching. Each agent's first 50 transactions get timestamped against a shared reference clock, producing a timing signature. Post-hoc clustering groups near-identical signatures; clusters above a size threshold are flagged. An attacker must stagger launch times and inject jitter per fake identity, raising operational cost per account beyond the payoff. A falcon agent farm run at zenith speed collapses into one cluster; slow juniper-paced seeding is expensive and slow.
